Tech Report: 'As late as my postman' - Brighton's European drama explained as VAR intervenes

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Universitatea Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off for standing on Matt O'Riley's ankle, at the Amex Stadium, on Thursday night (November 26).
  • The Romanian league leaders found themselves down to ten men in the 39th minute, with referee Matthias Jöllenbeck showing Screciu a red card as the first half approached its conclusion.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Universitatea Craiova defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off for standing on Matt O'Riley's ankle, at the Amex Stadium, on Thursday night (November 26).

The Romanian league leaders found themselves down to ten men in the 39th minute, with referee Matthias Jöllenbeck showing Screciu a red card as the first half approached its conclusion.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Screciu caught O'Riley on the foot, leaving the Brighton midfielder requiring lengthy treatment.

However, the incident initially went unnoticed by the referee, with play continuing on the other side of the pitch.

It was only after the officials became aware of the incident that the game was stopped and the decision reviewed by VAR.

In a recent development, warren Aspinall, former Brighton striker on BBC Sussex, said: “Vladimir Screciu's as late as my postman. He's off.

Recent findings suggest that “He's had a bad time, the second goal and now he's been sent off. I thought Matt O'Riley had just rolled it.”.

A stretcher was ready pitch-side but O'Riley was thankfully able to return to the pitch after receiving treatment.

The dismissal came with Brighton already holding a 2-0 lead, putting Fabian Hürzeler's side in a commanding position in their fourth Conference League league-phase fixture.

Ibrahim Osman had given Albion the perfect start, finding the net in the third minute after being set up by Jack Hinshelwood.

Maxim De Cuyper then doubled the advantage in the 33rd minute, leaving Craiova with a difficult task even before they lost one of their players.

What does the red card mean for Brighton?

For Hürzeler, the sending-off offered an opportunity to take greater control of proceedings.

With an extra player on the pitch, Brighton can look to stretch Craiova, move the ball across the pitch and exploit the spaces left by a side forced to defend with fewer players.

It also presents a chance to manage the game intelligently, particularly with a busy domestic schedule approaching.

In a recent development, aspinall remarked: “It's too easy, when they had 11 on and now it's worse. Craiova haven't offered anything; they're slow. They've played five at the back and we cut them open after three minutes.

It has been revealed that “I'd bring Lewis Dunk on, he could be like Tom Brady out there. They need the ball quicker; Pascal Struijk needs to do the same. They kept hitting the ball so hard it wasn't going to anybody.

Sources indicate that “Start showing you deserve this spot in the team, and give the manager a headache. If they don't score six or seven goals tonight, I'll be disappointed.”.

Aspinall wasn’t completely convinced by the first-half showing.

"The manager is having a go at some of these players, and rightly so,” he stated.

"Get your pass right and if you're playing like this against Newcastle on Sunday, they'll be in trouble.”.

Hürzeler made three changes at half-time, introducing Femi Azeez, Yasin Ayari and Costinha.

It was a particularly notable moment for Azeez, who made his Brighton debut after coming on as part of the triple substitution.

O'Riley, De Cuyper and Chema Andrés were the players withdrawn, with the Seagulls looking to manage their advantage and take control of the second half.

With Craiova down to ten men and Brighton already two goals ahead, the hosts are in an excellent position to secure another important European result.

Albion had arrived at the fixture looking to respond after their 2-0 defeat away to Hull City, and a convincing European performance would provide a welcome boost.

Both clubs had collected seven points from their opening three Conference League matches, making the meeting an key opportunity to strengthen their position in the league phase.

‘Very swollen’ - Fabian Hurzeler reveals fresh Brighton injury blow ahead of Newcastle after red card

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (468 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler gave a worrying injury upgrade for Matt O'Riley after the 4-0 win Conference League against Craiova.
  • O'Riley was clobbered in the 39th minute by visiting defender Vladimir Screciu, who was sent-off after VAR review.
  • Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler gave a worrying injury upgrade for Matt O'Riley after the 4-0 win Conference League against Craiova.

O'Riley was clobbered in the 39th minute by visiting defender Vladimir Screciu, who was sent-off after VAR review.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

It was a poor challenge from Screciu and one that saw O'Riley’s right ankle buckle into an unnatural position.

The Denmark international tried to play on but was replaced at halftime by debutant Femi Azeez.

"It did not look good," remarked head coach Hurzeler to Sussex World after the match. "It is very swollen. We will have to see.".

It's a blow for O'Riley who has had limited chances to impress this season.

The Denmark international has totalled just 370 minutes of action this season from nine appearances.

He's now highly unlikely to feature in the matchday squad to face Newcastle in the Premier League this Sunday.

Ibrahim Osman scored his first Brighton goals as his side returned to winning ways by cruising to a 4-0 success over 10-man Universitatea Craiova in the Conference League.

Talk of the high-flying Seagulls potentially being shock Premier League title contenders this season was dampened slightly by Sunday’s surprise 2-0 defeat at Hull.

Winger Osman finished a flowing move to set Albion on course to avoid a further unexpected defeat before Maxim De Cuyper superbly curled home his fifth goal of the campaign to double the lead.

Romanian champions Craiova were left with little hope of a comeback at the Amex Stadium when defender Vladimir Screciu was sent off in the 39th minute for stamping on the ankle of Matt O’Riley.

Osman set up Charalampos Kostoulas for the third goal before quickly claiming his second with a fine individual effort as Brighton made it 10 points from four games in the competition on a bitterly cold evening in Sussex.

“I think that was a really good start, and also very important to make the game look easy, because especially the first goal helped us force [the opponent] to open up the space,” he remarked.

Sources indicate that “That meant we could have more space to combine and more opportunity to attack their box. So I think we were very professional with good standards in the first half. Then, of course, the red card definitely helped us to finish - or to change - the structure of the game.

According to recent reports, “In the second half we created plenty of chances. I wasn't happy that we weren't clinical and clean enough finishing these chances, because I think we dropped our level a little bit there. Overall, though, winning 4–0 means that we did a lot of things well.”.

#221204. Wrexham vs Portsmouth - prediction, team news, lineups

Wrexham vs Portsmouth - prediction, team news, lineups

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:25.
  • Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.
  • Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 15:22, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:25.

Wrexham will look to extend their four-game unbeaten run when they welcome Portsmouth to the Racecourse Ground for Saturday’s Championship encounter.

Pompey, meanwhile, will be eyeing a second straight win after getting the better of West Ham United in midweek.

After overseeing just three wins in the first 13 league games, Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has eased some of the pressure that was building on his shoulders with a four-game unbeaten run.

Wrexham went into the international window on the back of a 2-0 win over Middlesbrough and a 1-1 draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, before they returned to action with a narrow 1-0 victory over Lincoln City at Sincil Bank.

They then took the lead in Tuesday’s away clash with Bristol City, but were ultimately forced to settle for a point after Joe Worrall saw his opener cancelled out by Cam Pring’s equaliser, leaving Wrexham in 14th spot in the Championship table and five points adrift of the top eight.

After playing back-to-back away games, Wrexham will be looking forward to returning to the familiar surroundings of the Racecourse Ground, where they have taken seven points from their last three outings since losing to West Bromwich Albion last month.

Wrexham are also one of six teams to score in every Championship home match this term, extending their overall run to at least one goal in each of their last 15 home league games since drawing a blank in a 2-0 loss to Millwall over seven months ago.

In fact, that scoring run includes a 2-1 victory in their recent meeting with Portsmouth in February, which came courtesy of first-half goals from Sam Smith and Max Cleworth.

Portsmouth, meanwhile, are just one point adrift of the playoffs after winning five, drawing three and losing just one of their last nine matches.

After losing to Stoke City before the international window, Pompey resumed their campaign with a hard-fought away draw against Bolton Wanderers before they claimed a 1-0 win in their first home meeting with West Ham United in 14 years.

Odin Bailey’s maiden Portsmouth goal proved enough to secure the club’s first head-to-head victory since a 1-0 success at Upton Park in April 2008, while also keeping their first home clean sheet since the start of September.

John Mousinho’s side will now head on their travels with hopes of extending their four-game unbeaten away run, which started with a 1-0 win over Norwich City and continued with three consecutive draws on the road.

No Championship team has conceded fewer away goals than Portsmouth, whose defence has been breached just six times in their eight road trips this season.

Given the fact they only took a point from their two meetings with Wrexham last term, Pompey will head into Saturday's fixture with hopes of claiming their first head-to-head league win since recording a 2-0 away victory in January 1983.

Wrexham forward Sam Smith will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining an anterior cruciate ligament injury earlier this month.

The hosts are also likely to be without the services of Liberato Cacace, Seb Revan, Josh Windass, Callum O’Hare and Nathan Broadhead.

Ollie Rathbone and Kieffer Moore - the latter of whom is Wrexham’s top scorer with five Championship goals to his name this term - are pushing for starting berths.

Jayden Meghoma will be out for up to 10 weeks after sustaining an ankle ligament injury in last weekend’s draw against Bolton.

Meghoma is the latest addition to a lengthy injury list that features Keshi Anderson, Luke Brooke-Smith, Marko Milovanovic, Colby Bishop, John Swift, Mark Kosznovszky, Connor Ogilvie and Benjamin Arthur.

Marlon Pack, Josh Murphy and Adrian Segecic are options to start if Mousinho decides to freshen up his side for Saturday’s away trip.

Wrexham possible starting lineup:.

Patterson; Cleworth, Worrall, Doyle; Kabore, Dobson, Whiteman, Ekomie; O’Brien, Rathbone; Moore.

Portsmouth possible starting lineup:.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Swanson; Pack, Mohamed; Segecic, Bailey, Murphy; Shade.

Portsmouth have conceded more than one goal in just one of their eight away league games this term, and with that in mind, we think they will do enough to avoid defeat in Saturday's fixture.

However, we believe they will fall short of claiming maximum points against a Wrexham side that are unbeaten in four games.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tomorrow’s game is significant for both AC Milan and Olympiacos, with both hoping to rise up the Europa League standings.

Sources indicate that for Milan, tomorrow is a must-win game. Of course, they all are, but they’re now at a stage where any defeat could seriously hinder their chances of qualification to the latter stages of the competition.

If they win all four of their final games, they’ll have a chance of a top eight finish, a slim one, but a chance nonetheless. However, a point would mean that they’ll likely have to settle for a top 24 spot.

With the squad thinning out, any possibility of avoiding extra games would be ideal for Ruben Amorim, but it will not be easy at all.

Speaking to the press before tomorrow’s game, Imanol Alguacil – Olympiacos’ head coach – looked at the strength of the Rossoneri, praise for Luka Modric and it being ‘life-or-death’ for both teams, as MilanPress relays.

“What if we change something? We’ll do it if necessary; I have no problem with that. I’ve already planned some things and we’ll adapt depending on the opponent. The same goes for Milan, we’ve done some tests and we’ll see how to approach the match.

In a recent development, “We’re not looking for excuses with the injuries in midfield, everyone is ready to play this game. Milan are strong; they’re one of the favourites to win the Europa League, even if they only have three points, and also Serie A.

Sources indicate that “We have great respect for them but also great ambition because we’ll be in front of our fans. It will be a life-or-death match for both us and them.”.

Both teams are struggling with injuries….

“Injuries happen, I’m not a coach who makes excuses. I brought some players up from the Primavera, but we want to make our fans happy. I want a team with character and I want everyone to give their all.

“Is Modric’s absence an advantage? It’s a shame he won’t be there because all coaches would like to play against the best players. All football fans would love to see someone like Modric play; I hope it’s nothing serious.

Sources indicate that “He’s done great things in Spain and he’s doing it with AC Milan too. What if I sign for a draw? We’re playing to win, then we’ll see at the end of the match what the fairest result was. We must treat AC Milan with respect because they’re a great team.”.

#221201. Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 35m • 📚 Deep Dive (6936 w)

Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 15:22, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 15:27.

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to make it three straight wins in all competitions when they continue their La Liga campaign against Elche on Saturday evening.

The Red and Whites have only been victorious in one of their last four games against Elche, with Los Franjiverdes enjoying the better of their recent meetings.

Elche have been victorious in two of their last four matches against Atletico, with those successes coming at home, including a 3-2 win in their last meeting in April of this year.

Los Franjiverdes will be the fresher of the two teams entering this match, with Atletico in Champions League action on Wednesday, but the hosts have only managed to pick up one point from the last nine available in Spain's top flight.

Martin Anselmi's side played out a 1-1 draw with Levante last time out, with that result following back-to-back defeats to Valencia and Real Betis.

Elche boast a record of two wins, five draws and six defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 11 points leaving them in 19th spot in the La Liga table.

Anselmi's team have the worst home record in Spain's top flight this season, having only managed to pick up one point from their six games in front of their own supporters.

Atletico, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-0 win over Viking in the Champions League on Wednesday, with Alexander Sorloth and Julian Alvarez on the scoresheet.

Simeone's side have a record of 10 wins, one draw and two defeats from their 13 matches in Spain's top flight this season, with 31 points leaving them in third spot in the table.

Atletico are only two points off second-placed Real Madrid and five from the leaders Barcelona, so they are firmly in a title race heading towards the start of December.

The Red and Whites recorded a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight last time out, with Simeone's team responding impressively to their 2-1 reverse to Barcelona before the November international break.

Atletico now have three straight league matches against Elche, Barcelona and Real Betis before returning to European action away to PSV Eindhoven on December 9.

Atletico Madrid form (all competitions):.

Elche are again expected to be without the services of Ruben Sanchez, Adam Boayar, Ali Houary, Marc Aguado and Yago Santiago due to injury problems.

Fer Nino has been in strong form for the hosts this season, scoring six goals in 13 appearances, and the 26-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There is also expected to be a spot in the attack for Abiel Osorio, who has one goal and one assist in 11 appearances for Elche during the current campaign.

As for Atletico, Ademola Lookman and Cristian Romero will again miss out due to injury problems, but the visitors are otherwise in strong shape, with no fresh challenges being reported following their Champions League clash with Viking.

Head coach Simeone is expected to introduce Pablo Barrios and Giuliano Simeone back into his starting side, with Sorloth and Lee Kang-in potentially dropping out.

Alvarez has only scored three times during a difficult season to date, with just one of those coming in Spain's top flight, but the Argentine should continue in the final third of the field.

Elche possible starting lineup:.

Dituro; Sangare, Redondo Solari, Chust, Revivo; Cepeda, Morcillo, Villar, Valera; Osorio, Nino.

Atletico Madrid possible starting lineup:.

Oblak; Llorente, Le Normand, Hancko, Grimaldo; Koke, Simeone, Barrios, Cardoso, Baena; Alvarez.

Elche's recent record against Atletico will hand them confidence ahead of this match, but we are expecting Simeone's side to navigate their way to an important three points.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scottish football chiefs have extended the consultation period for its intends to encourage the selection of more youngsters “with the intention of a comprehensive proposal within the first quarter of 2027” amid concerns from some major clubs.

The Scottish Football Association invited all 42 league clubs to a summit at St Andrews in early September, where they unveiled a package of proposals aimed at securing the future of the sport in Scotland.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The SFA wants a minimum of two Scottish under-21 players to be selected by each team in a Scottish Cup tie and for two Scottish under-21 players to be picked by each team in the Premier Sports Cup, starting from the 2027/28 campaign.

From next season as well, the SFA has also suggested under-21 players be on the pitch for an average of 60 minutes per game, across the season, in the Premiership, equating to six per cent of available minutes.

It has been revealed that led by recently-appointed chief football officer Craig Mulholland, the SFA had hoped to put some of their aims to a vote at the Scottish Professional Football League annual general meeting this month. With a downward trajectory of young Scottish players being selected in the Premiership over the past ten years, Mulholland stated in September that “we need to act now, otherwise we could end up finding ourselves in a crisis at some point in the future”.

The fear is that Scotland risks falling behind similarly-sized nations and will fail to qualify for major tournaments, while Premiership clubs were told by external firm Twenty First Group that they are leaving £40 million on the table in potential revenue by not placing more faith in academy players.

Nevertheless, The Scotsman understands that some of the SFA’s proposals have been met with scepticism from clubs across the leagues and the governing body has extended the consultation period “into the New Year” to continue dialogue on the best way forward.

A statement from the Scottish Football Association read: “The Scottish FA has been encouraged by the productive dialogue with clubs regarding proposals to harness opportunities for young homegrown talent.

“The most recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation in order to present a consolidated package of recommendations to an SPFL member vote.

“The passion we all have for Scottish football has been demonstrated by the public debate sparked since the all-club meeting in St Andrews, when the reality of our domestic game’s standing in respect of playing time for under-21 players compared to the rest of Europe was made clear.

“We will continue to engage in dialogue with the aim of delivering a proposal that will achieve the stated objective of improving opportunities for young homegrown players to fulfil their potential at the top end of the Scottish professional game.

“It is an objective everyone benefits from: players, clubs, supporters and Scotland national teams.

“We have therefore agreed that the consultation process will continue into the Latest Year with the intention of a comprehensive proposal going to SPFL members within the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of William Hill SPFL season 2027-28.

“The Scottish FA General Meeting to vote on the complementary Scottish Gas Men’s Scottish Cup proposals will now follow a similar timetable.

“Given the implications for our game, and our young talent, it is imperative that we take the necessary time to get those proposals right.”.

There was no grand gesture as Bradley Barcola walked back to the bench, just a high-five from Andoni Iraola and some of Liverpool’s coaching staff.

It was a similar situation as he left the stadium. Hood up, jacket zipped, baseball cap pulled on tightly, he politely turned down all requests to talk in English. “Not good enough,” he said with a smile, but that was the only thing that had not been up to standard.

Recent findings suggest that the giveaway here was what he held in his right hand – the match ball. On it were the signatures of Liverpool’s squad, congratulating him on a momentous performance that had arrived right on cue.

Recent findings suggest that if you are going end a barren spell, you do not want to just turn on the taps but burst the dam, and that is precisely what Barcola did on a wild night in Austria. He needed one goal to get his Liverpool career up and running, he ended up scoring three.

Iraola had remarked he was not concerned about Barcola’s numbers when Liverpool arrived in Linz, even if no goals and no assists since his £123m move from Paris St-Germain had caused debate, but those numbers look infinitely better now after his first senior hat-trick.

They made a difference. Bradley apart from the hat-trick I thought he was a threat.

“He was always one-on-one, certainly in behind and he helped us a lot to control the game, finding the pockets. I am happy for both of them, yes. For their confidence for sure, it’s very good. I think they feel now that we trust them a lot. It’s going to be very good for them.”.

Barcola should have had the stage to himself on an evening when Liverpool were so obviously better than LASK in Linz but it will have frustrated Iraola immensely that his team scoring six times was tarnished by three daft goals being given up in the final 25 minutes.

It has been revealed that the another good Barcola run is found, but his shot is screwed just wide of the near post. Barcola and Wirtz certainly more involved so far.

Industry observers note that diligent defending from Jorgenson to halt the progress of Barcola after a burst into the penalty area from the left. From the Liverpool corner, LASK goalkeeper Jungwirth was uncertain but Araujo could not not get enough on the header.

There really is something incongruous about seeing Kostas Tsimikas wearing the Liverpool captain’s armband. He should never have been given it again after throwing it on the floor after a pre-season friendly in the United States when he, Curtis Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai bickered with each other. The reason Alisson doesn’t wear it is because if there is a decision that requires him to talk to the referee in the opposition area, he would be miles from his own goal and potentially vulnerable. Alisson is the real leader on this pitch for this team.

Sources indicate that liverpool starting to turn their screw now. First, Wirtz skipped through a couple of challenges and fired a low shot straight at the goalkeeper before Ngumoha, playing on the right, drops a shoulder and drives to the byline, standing up a dangerous cross.

Then Wirtz tries another dribble through the middle, but his shot is charged down.

Liverpool struggling to clear their lines from the corner, and Schopf scoops a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Nyoni then tries a difficult reverse pass back towards Barcola but overcooks it. Moments before, there was a nice touch from Barcola to bring down a switch of play.

Lewis Koumas looking dangerous again, peeling behind LASK’s defence and rounding the goalkeeper Jungwirth on the corner of the penalty area, but he was forced wide and had to settle for a corner which the goalkeeper claims.

Recent findings suggest that then LASK pour forward again after a cheap giveaway by Araujo, and the home team win a corner of their own. Lively enough start.

Tsimikas scrambling rather to deal with a cross towards Jorgensen, before Alisson puts Liverpool under pressure with a stray pass, and LASK have a corner. Taken short, and then stood up to the back post but Liverpool clear.

It has been revealed that kostas Tsimikas captains Liverpool tonight, not words I ever expected to type but it is a team short of experience. Liverpool enjoying all of the possession so far, LASK are defending in a 5-2-3 shape, so Liverpool’s full-backs should have some time and space. Gravenberch does well to win a foul in midfield.

Liverpool get the game under way.

The home team play in all red, so Liverpool are in their white away strip. It looks like there is some Liverpool support among the locals/neutrals in the home end.

LASK XI: Jungwirth, Jorgensen, Mbuyamba, Alemao, Andrade, Dibango, Danek, Bogarde, Schopf, Lang, Adeniran.

Subs: Schutzenauer, Schillinger, Freckleton, Ljubicic, Kalajdzic, Verhaeghe, Elfadli, Flecker, Kane.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

Sources indicate that one novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola stated: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”.

Sources indicate that 24 - Liverpool's starting XI against LASK has an average age of 24 years and 186 days, their third-youngest ever for a UEFA Champions League game, older only than September 2001 v Borussia Dortmund (24y 136d) and December 2020 v Midtjylland (24y 26d). Knocks. https://t.co/4JeW73N87k.

Iraola makes four changes from the defeat by City so in come Frimpong, Tsimikas, Nyoni and Ngumoha.

Liverpool XI: Alisson, Frimpong, Araujo, Jacquet, Tsimikas, Nyoni, Gravenberch, Wirtz, Barcola, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Munoz, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Sonni-Lambie, Lucky.

Our team to take on LASK ✊ #UCL https://t.co/8vObg7mgLF.

Industry observers note that it is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”.

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

Recent findings suggest that they travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

In a recent development, tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” mentioned Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

Crawley extended their unbeaten run in the league under Blackwell to four games with a 0-0 draw at home to title contenders Barnet in midweek – and Blackwell now believes that his side are “competitive” – not only on the eye but also according to the data.

In a recent development, the former Sheffield United manager mentioned: “The data shows that we're very competitive now with sprints, decelerations, accelerations, high-speed runs. We're now coming at the top half of the table with that so it just shows that we've been improving all over.”.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

From a defensive point of view the past two games have shown a rejuvenated back-line – helped by the recent additions of Ben Heneghan and Josh Flint, which have made the Reds look a lot more resolute and solid.

According to recent reports, exeter are currently one spot below the play-off places sitting in 8th place on 23 points. The Grecians have the best defensive record in the league having only conceded 10 goals but Blackwell is not fazed by that.

He has communicated as much to his players: “It doesn't matter whether they're the top or the bottom, we feel now that we can compete with people, and that's all I wanted to do, make us competitive. Then hopefully Lady Luck smiles on you on the day and you can get some good results.”.

Blackwell was pleased that more players have stepped up to the mark to give him more confidence in choices.

He said: “We talk about how any team wants to be competitive from 1-22 really, and know that if you lose a player, that someone can seamlessly step in. What was pleasing was that we made some changes, shifted it around a little bit, and then whoever we brought in did a good job, so that gives me more power.”.

With the Reds involved in a lunchtime kick-off, Blackwell was asked whether that makes a difference to the way they approach the game.

He replied: “I think it's something that I've been used to now for the last 15 years, you know, being in a Championship or the Premier League and abroad in Poland is exactly the same.

“You don't know whether you're playing a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday or a Monday, they're the four days that you normally play.

It has been revealed that “You don't know whether you're going to be at 12 o'clock, 2pm, 4pm, 8pm – so it's now it's just normal for players; it certainly has been for me. So nothing different, whatever the time is, we'll prepare as if it were a 3pm kick-off or a 1pm kick-off. Preparation is the same.”.

Eight goals at Dens Park is one thing. Going toe-to-toe with French aristocrats and being beaten, cruelly, at the death is quite another. Hearts’ growing reputation as the great entertainers was nevertheless burnished here in thrilling fashion.

Sources indicate that the price the Hearts fans might have to pay for such swashbuckling play was also demonstrated. Defensive fragility was all too apparent, including at the end when substitute Mamadou Coulibaly brushed off a challenge in midfield and threaded the ball through for Folarin Balogun to score his second and the night’s decisive goal. We were already into the final minute of the four added on at the end of a quite breathless European tie.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Mon Dieu! What a match. AS Monaco won’t forget this trip to Scotland, and a vibrant Tynecastle, in a hurry. As for the hosts, they remain just about alive in the Conference League.

Sources indicate that the point they were deprived in heartbreaking fashion would have made such a difference. As good as Monaco are, it wasn’t as if Hearts were undone by a moment of genius, which makes it harder to bear. The hosts also had chances to score their own third goal and were angered when referee Daniel Schlager waved away penalty appeals when substitute Josh McPake ended up in a heap after Jordan Teze’s challenge.

Industry observers note that perhaps the home supporters will simply have to put up with see-sawing emotions in a season that’s already shaping up to be one of the craziest in the club’s history. Perhaps defensive slackness, although costly, must simply be endured if goals continue to flow at the other end, especially ones as sensational as Hearts fans were treated to here. Drop them off in the Louvre on your way home, Monaco.

Jordi Altena’s opener was declared a “potential” goal of the season by the always judicious Tynecastle Tannoy announcer. Just as well because a better one was just around the corner. Sabah Kerjota’s curler on the stroke of half time was an immaculate finish that Lukas Hradecky, the experienced keeper, just had to stand rooted to his spot and admire.

It has been revealed that altena’s strike was not quite in the same unsavable part of the goal but it was still breathtaking in its execution. Kerjota, the little Albanian livewire, also played a part in it. His free-kick looked to be going in until Hradecky pushed the ball against the post. Claudio Braga made sure the ball was recycled and played it back to Kerjota, who passed it inside to Altena. The Dutchman is fast becoming a Tynecastle favourite. No wonder when he can strike a ball like this. Hradecky was left flapping at the air beneath his bar.

It has been revealed that since going 5-0 down to Falkirk after 47 minutes earlier this month at Tynecastle, Hearts had scored 10 unanswered goals. This was the 11th. The response was always coming. This was AS Monaco after all. They might be struggling currently in Ligue 1 but how can they be they be written off? The team remains packed full of talent. This was not the shadow side Hearts might have hoped to face. Eric Dier, the England international, was present and correct as was former Arsenal player – and Donald Trump’s friend - Balogun.

Monaco were the ones raising a quizzical French eyebrow at the home team sheet. Due to much publicised injury problems and lack of adequate club-trained academy players, Hearts couldn’t even fill the bench.

Matthew Gillies stepped in for his first senior start in midfield. Unless Monaco were familiar with Stenhousemuir's opening matches of this season, the talented 19-year-old might have been something of a mystery to them. The same applies to Finlay Pollock, who is something of a mystery to Hearts fans as well.

Recent findings suggest that pollock came on towards the end for his first Hearts appearance since 2024. The 22-year-old has been out on loan at East Fife and Raith Rovers in between times. He was given the last nine minutes in place of a drained Kerjota. The whole team, including substitutes, looked shattered at the end but they had contributed to a game that will live long in the memory. There was the drama of an overturned penalty for Hearts in the second half after an alleged handball by substitute Mathys Detourbet as well as the sight of Beau Reus galloping up field for a corner in the final seconds.

The visitors’ first goal of the night saw Balogun do the necessary – and no more - from the penalty spot after Stuart Findlay had clipped the heels of the dangerous Matthis Abline.

Recent findings suggest that there was some dismay among home fans about Reus’ lack of movement. Balogun’s penalty lacked conviction and certainly wasn’t placed in the corner. Far from it. Nevertheless, it brought Monaco level. The French side took heart although they didn’t have it all their own way. Abline was booked for a foul on Laurent Mendy as Hearts forced the visitors into sometimes desperate measures.

According to recent reports, monaco did though take the lead for the first time in the night five minutes before half time after Edan Diop took advantage of a slack ball from Altena following a throw-in. After playing a one-two with Balogun, he slipped the ball beyond Reus.

Gillies was showing his worth in midfield. He might have had a goal to tell his pals about had Pierre Landry Kabore not taken the ball off his foot as he was preparing to unleash a shot from the edge of the box. Kabore, following his brace against Dundee, was in frisky form but often got a little too excited and forgot the basics, such as avoiding running into teammates.

Sources indicate that gillies was withdrawn at half time for Blair Spittal, back from injury and desperate to play a part. He also took the captain’s armband from McCart and helped drive Hearts on. Sadly, his and others’ efforts were in vain on an agonising night for the hosts.

Recent findings suggest that the club’s decision to go for a change at the top has caused a huge amount of upset – with many fans saying it is a shocking decision and a number of Macdonald’s squad deciding to follow him out of the door. And it is the way the decision appears to have been handled that has caused the most anger.

As the week unfolded, Town – who are second from bottom of the Isthmian South East division after only two wins in 19 games – appointed club stalwart Dave Winterton as interim manager, with senior player Arron Hopkinson assisting him, and asked fans to get behind him.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

And they put out an advert inviting applicants for the job, with talk of them wanting to take the whole club – not just the men’s first team – forward as one.

Macdonald’s right-hand man Ben Davis has gone in the wake of the sacking and so, reportedly, have long-serving Adam Davidson and at least five players.

Macdonald gave an exclusive interview to the Eastbourne Herald and sussexworld.co.uk in which he remarked he had been told eight days before he was sacked that his job was ‘bomb-proof’ all the time the chairman was in place.

According to recent reports, he also stated he had learned the club had decided they wanted a change of manager on November 16 – and only after two more games, training and two more siginings did they tell him. Macdonald told us he was asked if would resign, but refused.

You can read our full interview with Macdonald, who has been at the helm since 2022, on pages 62 & 63. He finished it with these words: “You don’t often get the chance to manage the club from the town you grew up in and I’ve just committed over 10% of my life to it, so the next few days and weeks will just be reflecting on that and appreciating the opportunity that the club gave me four-and-a-half years ago, and the continued and consistent success we have given them in return.”.

As for what happens next, Winterton isinterim manager and the Town committee have asked fans to get behind him as he guides the squad through what will be a tricky period.

The immediate aim is to try to get out of the Isthmian SE danger zone, and that starts with a visit to Erith Town tomorrow, followed by a home Sussex derby with Broadbridge Heath a week later.

Those won’t be easy games with a number of Macdonald’s players announcing they also left – including James Waters, who had only rejoined the club a day before the manager was ousted.

Industry observers note that meanwhile the club – who gave ‘sincere thanks’ to Macdonald in their statement revealing he was leaving – are inviting applicants for the vacancy. They stated: “We are looking for an individual who shares our ambition, understands the importance of building a strong club culture and is passionate about developing players, creating opportunities and delivering success both on and off the pitch.

Industry observers note that "At Eastbourne Town, we believe the First Team should be an vital part of a wider football development pathway. We want to create an environment where young players can see a realistic route from youth football through U18 and U23 football and ultimately into the first team.”.

Read the stories from Town’s turbulent week in today’s Eastbourne Herald.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Darren Plant | 26 Nov 2026 15:41.

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has revealed that Moises Caicedo is available for Friday's Premier League fixture against Nottingham Forest.

The Ecuador international has found himself in and out of the Blues starting lineup this season due to several fitness challenges.

Caicedo's latest injury came during the first half of last weekend's game versus Leeds United, the midfielder landing awkwardly on his back and needing to be withdrawn.

As a result, Caicedo has been an obvious injury doubt for what is a potentially-crucial game for Alonso after three defeats in four top-flight games.

However, speaking at his pre-match press conference, the Spaniard declared Caicedo available for selection.

He told reporters: "Yes, he's going to be OK for tomorrow.".

On a negative note, Alonso acknowledged that Joao Pedro would remain sidelined for the trip to the East Midlands.

Meanwhile, providing an update on Maxence Lacroix's hamstring injury, he added: "It's one less week than the last game so we are closer to recovery but not for this game.".

There have been reports which suggest that Lacroix could return earlier than the initial target return period of January.

With Lacroix still injured, Alonso may feel forced to start Wesley Fofana alongside Levi Colwill, despite being furious with the Frenchman's comments in an interview this week.

There is the possibility of Josh Acheampong starting in the centre with Colwill, with Marco Palestra potentially starting at right-back.

If Jorrel Hato remains sidelined with a back injury, Pep Chavarria is favourite to start at left-back.

Alonso also has the option of going with a back three featuring the aforementioned centre-backs, with Pedro Neto at right wing-back and Palestra on the left.

THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect

  • Recent findings suggest that ‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ noted Carragher post-match.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 21:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:37 EST, 25 November 2026.

After Florian Wirtz trudged off the field just over an hour into Liverpool’s defeat by Manchester City in October, sacrificed following Ryan Gravenberch’s red card, Jamie Carragher had once again seen enough of the £116million man.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ noted Carragher post-match. ‘I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again.’.

Fast forward six weeks, and Wirtz was running the show for Liverpool as they put four past Manchester United in poor Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, topping a stellar performance off with a goal and an assist. Carragher hailed the German’s stunning first-half volley as ‘a goal Dennis Bergkamp would have scored’.

Industry observers note that how things change. This was a performance, even against an abysmal 10-man United, that highlighted Wirtz was ready, at last, to seize the major occasions.

It has been revealed that because, for so long, he wasn’t ready. Carragher was not alone in his earlier assessment, one shared by countless frustrated Liverpool fans. There was a feeling that this slight, wispy technician had the tools to flourish in the slower-paced Bundesliga, or even for Liverpool in the Champions League, but would, perhaps, remain unable to shine amid the rough and tumble of the Premier League.

According to recent reports, wirtz managed five goals and four assists in the Premier League last season and added only one assist this term before that City game. Since then, he’s come to life. Four assists and a couple of goals in the league with another one of each in the Champions League, a tally he will hope to add to on Wednesday evening against Club Bruges.

Florian Wirtz has suddenly sprung to life as a Liverpool player and is making his critics eat their words.

Wirtz scores a majestic flick against Manchester United on Sunday.

Since that City defeat, Wirtz is getting into dangerous positions more often. He is having more touches in the opposition box, more shots in the opposition box, playing more passes into the opposition box and creating more than twice as many chances from open play.

Wirtz boasts a league-high 29 of those this season, and 20 of the chances have come since that City game.

According to recent reports, the last player to create more than the 10 open-play chances Wirtz managed against United was David Silva in 2015. Wirtz created nine against Brentford, too, in the first league match after the City defeat, meaning he’s the only Premier League player on record (since 2003-04) to create nine or more chances from open play in multiple games in the same season. Wirtz did it twice in five weeks.

It has been revealed that let’s nip this one in the bud early. It is clear, of course, that Jurgen Klopp, the legendary former Liverpool manager now Germany head coach, has got a tune out of Wirtz in recent months. The pair, according to those who follow the national team, are very close.

‘Wirtz is a once-in-a-century talent,’ was Klopp’s assessment last year, while he later remarked that he was ‘shocked’ by how good Wirtz was in their first training session together.

The 23-year-old has shown it in matches, too, with four goals and an assist in his last four games for Germany, including a brace last week against the Netherlands.

This has fed a narrative of how Klopp has been the one to unlock Wirtz’s powers. Klopp deserves credit, naturally, but he is also helped by having the freedom to give Wirtz what he needs: space.

It has been revealed that ‘What do I need to be at my best? Ideally, a lot of space in every game so I can do what I want!’ stated Wirtz after scoring one and setting up the other in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia in October.

Industry observers note that he was half-joking, laughing as he said it, but he’s right. Technical creators like Wirtz thrive on space. He’s been able to have more of that in international football, with Klopp even playing him as a false nine to give him all the creative freedom he needs. He leads the press but the midfielders behind him do the bulk of the dirty work to allow Wirtz, the star, to shine.

Wirtz’s performances with his country have helped grow his confidence, but it would be deeply unfair on Iraola to suggest Klopp’s blueprint is the one now being copied.

WIRTZ HAS ALWAYS BEEN IRAOLA’S MAN.

Even if Liverpool and Germany play a similar style, it is much, much harder to give players freedom in the Premier League.

But if anyone was going to find a way to do it for Wirtz, it was Iraola.

Industry observers note that arne Slot could never work it out. By the end of his tenure, he’d played Wirtz as an attacking midfielder, stuck him on both flanks and thrust him up front. It was a conundrum he just couldn’t solve.

Iraola's Bournemouth side were one of the hardest-working, highest-pressing teams in the division but his system was still able to allow the likes of Justin Kluivert or Junior Kroupi to create and drift into pockets of space to set the attacking tempo.

For Iraola, it was always going to be Wirtz. The German has started every league game, all of them in the No 10 position.

He’s always led the way off the ball – only three players have won possession more often in the final third this season – but Iraola has been finding different ways to get the best out of him with the ball, too. Against Brentford, he shifted Rio Ngumoha inside almost to play as a second No 10 beside Wirtz, which helped create space for him to set up Liverpool's equaliser.

Having Alexis Mac Allister behind him allows Wirtz to concentrate on being the creative heartbeat, while even Dominik Szoboszlai has played noticeably deeper since returning from injury.

Andoni Iraola has started Wirtz in every league game, all of them in the No 10 position.

ISAK PARTNERSHIP STARTING TO BLOSSOM.

Recent findings suggest that szoboszlai isn't the only one. Another aspect of Germany's game that has helped Wirtz is lining up alongside strikers who like to drop deep in Kai Havertz and Nick Woltemade, leaving space for Wirtz to attack.

Recent findings suggest that in recent weeks, especially against United, Liverpool striker Alexander Isak has been doing the same. It was Isak doing exactly that which led to Wirtz’s goal.

Isak (below, in possession) drops in, plays the ball out wide to Ngumoha and Wirtz sprints into the box to get on to the end of the cross.

Alexander Isak dropped into midfield and sprayed the ball wide to Rio Ngumoha before Wirtz's goal against United.

Isak missed much of last season through injury but his all-round play is much better attuned to Wirtz's game than those who played alongside him for most of 2025-26, including Hugo Ekitike.

One of the most devastating aspects of Iraola’s Bournemouth was how rapidly players flooded forward when they attacked.

His Liverpool side is starting to do the same which, in turn, helps get the best out of Wirtz.

Last season under Slot, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Mo Salah would often tuck in instead of bombing forward out wide and Milos Kerkez, one of the most attacking full backs in the division under Iraola at Bournemouth, rarely did the same under Slot.

Sources indicate that now, Liverpool’s wingers are flying. This season under Iraola, Liverpool are averaging more ‘fast breaks’, how Opta define counter attacks, and shots from them than in any campaign under Slot or even the ‘heavy metal’ Klopp.

According to recent reports, wirtz has attempted seven through balls this season, one of the highest tallies in the division. Since the City game in particular, he has tried to play passes with purpose into the box.

Wirtz was creating chances in the first six games of this season but only a few of them were penetrating passes into the box.

The German's chances created in the last five games, since the City defeat, show how many balls he is playing into dangerous areas.

The rapid Bradley Barcola starting to find his feet since his £123m move has been a huge help to Wirtz.

Of Wirtz’s 20 open-play chances created since the City game, a quarter of them have been for Barcola.

Having those runners out wide like Barcola and Ngumoha is so helpful for the German. As he drives forward with the ball against United (below), he has three runners ahead of him with even Szoboszlai bursting forward. Wirtz has so many options and eventually slips in Isak for a great chance.

Liverpool had wide runners driving forward against United, helping Wirtz create chances and split their defence.

You can see from the average position map from the game (below), just how attacking Liverpool’s wingers – and Kerkez – were, albeit, granted, against 10 men for most of the contest.

The average position map of Liverpool's players against United indicates how high up the pitch they played.

Wirtz has had a run like this before, around this time last year. During December and January, he racked up four league goals and three assists – having not managed a single one until then – only to notch one of each for the rest of the Premier League campaign.

You get the sense, though, with his confidence growing under managers for both club and country who want to play his way, that he might just keep shining this time.

Since taking over, the Reds are unbeaten in four in the league, and despite dropping out of both cup competitions in the space of three days, there has been a mentality shift in the players – and the fans have seen that the players are giving their all.

Despite Christmas just being around the corner, the club hope Reds fans travel in their numbers to Exter to cheer the boys on in an early kick off. But it has been noted that Blackwell doesn’t celebrate with the players like past managers have.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking in his pre-Exeter press conference, Blackwell mentioned one or two fans asked him why he didn’t go and thank the support: “I thank the fans all the time, but after the game, it’s important that the players get the credit, not the manager.

Sources indicate that “That’s not my job. My job is to try to prepare the team, and the players go out and give everything. If they do that, that’s what the fans want. They don’t want me walking up and down the pitch clapping and whatever. Get on, do your job Blackwell, do your job. And if that’s the case, the players are doing well.”.

Industry observers note that he added: “It’s not my style. I enjoy them enjoying it and I enjoy that the fans enjoy it. I’ve had a great career, managing significant clubs and been a long way in big competitions, been all over the world, and I’ve never wanted the adulation.

“I just enjoy other people having it and seeing my players get that and the fans enjoying it. Sending them home after a week’s work, seeing the players give everything. That’s what they want. If we can keep doing that, I think we keep them on-side.”.

Talking about the bond between players and fans, Blackwell said “I want the players to take the credit because the bond is between the players and the fans, and that’s the bond.

Recent findings suggest that "As an ex-player, I knew there was a great bond between me and the fans. I’d hate to think that the manager walked up and started taking my thunder after having a man of the match performance and he walks up and takes all the credit. No, I want the players to have the credit.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wouter Vrancken has stressed Hearts’ objective remains the same despite conceding a last-minute goal that led to an agonising defeat against AS Monaco at Tynecastle.

Hearts’ hopes of reaching the knockout stage rest on winning their last two Conference League matches against Bosnian side Borac Banja Luca and Cypriot team Pafos, probably by high-scoring margins.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Tynecastle manager was not giving up on anything after the 3-2 loss, with United States World Cup star Folarin Balogun scoring the winning goal in the final seconds of added time.

Hearts had taken the lead after a sensational strike from Jordi Altena on 15 minutes. A penalty from Balogun levelled things before the visitors took the lead with a goal from Edam Diop five minutes before half time. Sabah Kerjota scored the goal of the night on the stroke of half-time after curling in with his left foot to leave everything to play for in the second half.

Recent findings suggest that “I think the point doesn't make a difference,” said Vrancken. “There's also something that really was pleasing for me is that when it was 2-2, we still wanted to go (for the win).

Sources indicate that "You saw also when it was a throw-in, we wanted to do it fast, we wanted to go for the win. Against a side like this, in the situation we're in, I am so really proud of this also.

"Three points would make a difference," he added. "Zero or one point doesn't make a difference towards the next games, so you have to win the next games. One point or no points doesn't change anything in the next games.”.

The Belgian stressed his pride in his players and reiterated that Hearts were missing nine injured players as well as Leart Kabashi and Eduardo Ageu, who were not named in the European squad. He did, however, lament the lack of concentration that saw them concede so late in the game after 93-and-a-half minutes of lung-busting effort. He was also unhappy that Hearts were not cute enough to stop Monaco in their tracks as they broke free for the winning goal. Substitute Finlay Pollock had the chance to clip Mamadou Coulibaly’s heels before the midfielder played in Balogun. Ruthlessness might be something Hearts are lacking at this level. A reporter pointed out that it was a cruel way to lose a match.

In a recent development, “It did feel like this,” remarked Vrancken. “But at the same time, we have to learn in that situation because I think until then we were really solid about giving chances away. And I expect more from guys who come in from the side (substitutes).

Industry observers note that “We can win it with a fresh player and in the middle we can win it with a fresh player. Or you make a foul somewhere to keep the result - I expect this. This is like battling for the team, as I call it.

Sources indicate that “We have to do better there,” he added. “But the biggest thing, of course, is to be really proud of what performance we put on the park today, because it's against a really good side. Knowing that we have still nine injuries - I will name it - and we have a lot of players not on the European list today and still do this against that team. I'm really proud of what we did.”.

Industry observers note that he hailed the quality of his side’s goals. “You see also the confidence those guys have. This is what we wanted after the weekend, of course - that you take some confidence from the dynamics of what we did there. I think the conviction around the box was there, in both boxes actually. It's an notable thing to take with us towards the next games coming, especially in this run of games.”.

Hearts host Celtic, who beat them 7-1 last month, at Tynecastle on Sunday. Vrancken is firmly in the belief that his side have their mojo back following this and the 5-2 defeat to Falkirk earlier this month. Hearts have since beaten Dundee 8-0 and been edged out by Monaco in a five-goal thriller. “We have played two good games and two good performances against good sides, especially today,” he mentioned. “And now you have the confidence. But we are still playing against a good side on Sunday with only two days' rest, so we have to manage fatigue and make sure that we are as fresh as possible again to make up for something a few weeks ago, especially because it's an at-home game.”.

Recent findings suggest that monaco manager Filipe Luis, meanwhile, denied that relief was the primary emotion after leaving it so late to collect three points. “It is not relief, we compete to win,” he said. “We had an amazing opportunity to win tonight but we had a tough opponent.

“They scored two unbelievable goals,” he added. “You almost need to applaud them. When a team scores two goals like this it is almost nobody’s fault. They are two fantastic goals. Honestly, it’s very beautiful.”.

Sources indicate that he spoke admiringly of the atmosphere. “I played against Celtic (with Atletico Madrid) in 2011 I think in the Europa League,” he said. “We are lucky to have the opportunity to play these types of games in different countries. It is so intense. I am happy to have had this opportunity to be here tonight – and happy with the result.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AC Milan will make the trip to Greece with the hopes of turning a corner against Olympiacos after a rough start to their Europa League campaign.

It has been a tale of two competitions this season so far for Milan. In Serie A they are inside the top four and have won eight games out of 12, leading to suggestions of a Scudetto bid. However, in Europe they have lost three of four, and sit in the bottom eight.

It has been revealed that it means that they’ll have to be perfect to even be in with a chance of a top eight finish – given you’ve needed at least 15 points in the last two seasons. Nevertheless, a point and gaining a bit of momentum across all competitions would still be appreciated.

Game date: Thursday, November 26 Kick-off time: 18:45 (CET) Venue: Karaiskakis Stadium Referee: Chris Kavanagh (VAR: Bankes).

As mentioned, things have been going quite well for Milan domestically. Sunday’s 5-1 victory against surprise package Frosinone was another example of the potential of this team, but there remains a necessity to find some consistency.

This is especially the case when it comes to the Europa League, in which the Rossoneri have been quire frankly awful. A 4-0 win against RB Salzburg in round two was the only glimmer of light, with the other three games being defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros, all without scoring.

As things stand right now, Milan would not even make the play-off spots as they sit outside the top 24. There is only one point in it and even eighth is only four points away, though the runway is getting shorter with only 12 points to play for.

Recent findings suggest that the result of this is that Amorim is expected to name quite a strong side for the game, but we must start with the injury absences. The big doubt is Strahinja Pavlovic, who needs another check on a kidney stone problem despite playing 20 minutes off the bench against Frosinone.

Alexis Saelemaekers, Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Pietro Terracciano and Ruben Loftus-Cheek have all missed the past few games due to various problems and will not be available on Thursday either.

Recent findings suggest that on Tuesday, the news broke that Milan will be without Luka Modric, who felt a tweak in his right thigh during the last game. The Croatian will be given Thursday night to recover and potentially the Cagliari game too, with the hopes of having him back at the start of December. Then, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi have already been ruled out.

The other bit of news is that Fikayo Tomori returned to training on Wednesday, which is a big boost given how thin the options are in defence, but it remains to be seen if the Englishman is deemed fit enough to play a part after his absence.

With the squad running quite thin, Amorim won’t have many options to rotate, nor does he have the luxury to with the standings.

Industry observers note that nevertheless, there will be one at the back, where Pervis Estupinan is expected to start. Mike Maignan starts behind Sankhoun Diawara and Koni De Winter, with Mario Gila at right-back again.

In a recent development, modric’s injury means Ardon Jashari will be given a chance on Thursday, and it’s one he must take. Alongside him, he’ll be covered with reliability from Yunus Musah and Adrien Rabiot, which should help.

Finally, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are expected to start on the flanks, with Goncalo Ramos through the middle.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Estupinan; Musah, Jashari, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Sources indicate that predicted bench: Bouyer, Torriani, F. Terracciano, M. Cissé, Tomori, Perera, Comotto, Vos, Ossola, Hutchinson, Cisse, Menon.

According to recent reports, injuries & suspensions: Saelemaekers, P. Terracciano, Gabbia, Chukwueze, Loftus-Cheek, Modric, Pavlovic, Camarda, Bartesaghi.

According to recent reports, olympiacos came into the upcoming season having had a mixed 2025-26 campaign under Jose Luis Mendilibar. They finished runners-up to city rivals AEK Athens in the Greek Super League and lost in the Greek Cup quarter-finals, but won the Super Cup and got to the knockout stage play-offs in the Champions League.

Recent findings suggest that in the summer window, the Erythrolefkoi spent over €78m on signings. The headline additions were midfielder Gustavo Puerta from Racing Santander for €16m, centre-back David Carmo rom Nottingham Forest for €9m and striker Armando Gonzalez from Chivas for €8.6m.

They also spent sums between €5-7m on striker Marius Mouandilmadji, right-back Marcus Pedersen, winger Leon Bailey, left-back Nair Tiknizyan, winger Joel Roca and centre-back Zinedin Smajlovic.

It has been revealed that the spending was almost totally offset by four major sales. Goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis went to Hull City for €23.3m, winger Andre Luis headed to Kansas City for €15.5m, midfielder Christos Mouzakitis also joined Hill for €15, and full-back Costinha was bought by Brighton for €12.7m.

It has been revealed that mandilibar would only last until September 9 before being replaced by Imanol Alguacil as the new head coach. Faith had been waning since the 2-1 aggregate loss to NEC in the Champions League third qualifying round, and the change came after a 1-1 draw with Volos.

According to recent reports, olympiacos are currently second in the league table with 26 points from 11 games, via eight wins, two draws and one defeat. They have scored 22 goals and allowed only seven, trailing the current leaders Panathinaikos by four points. They are three ahead of AEK, who have a game in hand and a better goal difference.

According to recent reports, in the Europa League, they have been exceptional so far. They beat Jagellonia Bialystok 2-1 at home, Marseille 1-0 away, Sparta Praha 1-0 at home and drew 0-0 away with Stade Rennais. That puts them sixth in the table, and within striking distance of top.

According to recent reports, in terms of injury news, Olympiacos are expected to be without forwards Ayoub El Kaabi, Yusuf Yazici (who has a Europa League hat-trick against Milan, for Lille) and Chiquino. Midfielders Gustavo Puerta and Santiago Hezze are out, while Leon Bailey may be the latest to join the treatment room as per reports.

Industry observers note that in defence, a few changes are expected, especially after conceding twice at the weekend. So, Ortega, Saliakas and Restos keep their spots. However, Carmo and Onyemaechi are expected to start.

Moving into midfield, the pivot won’t be touched, with Scipioni and former Bologna man Remo Freuler keeping their spots with Silva starting ahead of them.

It seems Leon Bailey may be given the nod on the right, despite the medical challenges, whilst Fortounis will continue on the left of the attacking quartet behind Gonzalez.

Predicted Olympiacos XI vs AC Milan (4-2-3-1): Ortega; Saliakas, Retsos, Carmo, Onyemaechi; Freuler, Scipioni; Bailey, Silva, Fortounis; Gonzalez.

Predicted bench: Stournaras, Georgakopoulos, Smajlovic, Pirola, Toufakis, Pedersen, Martins, Yaremchuk, Tiknizyan, Bruno, Sa.

Injuries & suspensions: El Kaabi, Yazici, Chiquinho, Puerta, Hezze.

AC Milan and Olympiacos have faced each other four times. Two came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19, which means that the meetings were almost 60 years apart.

In a recent development, in the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

Industry observers note that the most recent encounters were eight years ago as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

Industry observers note that ➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

In a recent development, ➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

Recent findings suggest that ➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

It has been revealed that ➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

It has been revealed that ➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

Industry observers note that ➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

Starting in midfield, the obvious choice here is Ardon Jashari. This has been called his game by the Italian media and it’s tough to disagree. If he’s going to have a future with the club beyond this season, a strong start tomorrow is imperative.

The other obvious choice is Pervis Estupinan. The Ecuadorian is a late entry into the expected XI, despite reports linking him with a potential exit in January. Bartesaghi’s injury means he’ll be given a chance and maybe, just maybe, it’s not too late for him. Something of promise needs to be seen, though.

In a recent development, with Milan lacking Modric in their midfield, it could allow someone like Remo Freuler to take the game by his pace. He’s got plenty of European experience and with the Rossoneri likely to rely on Jashari to set the pace, he may take the edge.

Then, if Leon Bailey starts, he’ll be the major threat of the night. Facing Estupinan and Diawara, he’ll have the opportunity to face a duo that have no relation yet. If he catches them out, it could be a long night for the Diavolo.

In a recent development, it’s been a real case of Jekyll and Hyde for Milan in the Europa League, to the point where it’s tough to call which side we’ll see. Logically, after such a heavy win at the weekend, the visitors should be coming away with three points.

However, both teams aren’t brilliant defensively and it could become an open game as a result. Considering what’s at stake, though, the Rossoneri may just edge past the hosts, but it won’t be easy….

Kilmarnock's biggest weakness has undeniably been their defensive vulnerability, having conceded 33 goals in 14 league matches - seven more than any other team in the division.
