Paul Pogba believes Manchester United should follow Arsenal’s blueprint under Mikel Arteta and has accused his former club of living in the past.

United decided to sack Michael Carrick during the international break and have brought in Mauricio Pochettino to deliver an immediate turnaround after a poor start to the season.

Pochettino suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge and that was followed by a 2-2 draw away to Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

United have not won a trophy in their last two seasons and Pochettino’s side are now in an early relegation battle as they sit 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 games.

Pogba, meanwhile, has endorsed Pochettino’s move to Old Trafford but feels United need to look at Arsenal’s return to the top as a model to follow.

Industry observers note that ‘I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he’s a great manager. And I’m sad also for Michael Carrick because I don’t think he had enough time to show and prove himself,’ Pogba told talkSPORT.

In a recent development, ‘But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there’s a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win and we all think that they should change manager.

‘All I think about this team, I’ve been there, is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside.

‘Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things.

‘The players also have to perform, have to understand the manager. And this way, they can go somewhere, like Arsenal.

Recent findings suggest that ‘But the pressure, I know it’s a major club, it’s Manchester United, was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have held talks over a January move for Fulham defender Calvin Bassey.

United’s defence shipped another four goals last weekend against Liverpool with only Crystal Palace conceding more in the Premier League this season.

With the club slumped in 19th place after 11 games, Mauricio Pochettino will be backed in the January transfer window with a centre-half, a left-back and a striker targeted.

While they are also interested in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Brentford star Nathan Collins, Bassey has emerged as a leading target for United.

His current contract at Craven Cottage expires in the summer with Fulham holding the option to extend that by a further 12 months.

The Cottagers are also in active talks with their captain over a new contract. But United remain hopeful of prising him away from west London with The Athletic reporting talks are taking place to ‘understand the conditions’ of a January move.

Bassey turned in another fine performance as Fulham held Manchester City to a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Speaking after the game, the former Rangers star was asked about his future, telling TNT Sports: ‘Of course [it is something we want to get done quickly.].

It has been revealed that ‘We are negotiating, we are still talking. It’s an amazing place to be, I have settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. It’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United are also looking at signing a left-back with Sporting CP star Maxi Araujo one option. Alejandro Balde is also open to a move with his first-team prospects at Barcelona not improving since the summer.

In a recent development, up front, the Athletic report United are not expected to make a move for Monaco and USA forward Folarin Balogun. Dominic Calvert-Lewin was also of interest but he has now signed a new contract with Leeds United.

Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2149 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

Sources indicate that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Sandro Tonali has hailed Tottenham team-mate Destiny Udogie as “one of the best” left-backs.

The Italian pair were already familiar with one another before Tonali’s substantial-money move to north London from Newcastle United in the summer for a fee worth £100million.

They had first played together in at Under-21 level on the international stage, before reuniting for the senior Azzurri side and at club level.

Udogie, who was told by manager Roberto De Zerbi what he must do to start more games, was given the nod from the off against Ipswich Town last time out, as Spurs won 2-0 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The left-back impressed behind Luca Williams-Barnett, with the young star netting his first goal for the club on his first senior start.

Udogie, meanwhile, was making just his fifth start of the campaign amid injury problems.

He has also had to contend with former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson arriving to add competition in his position after Djed Spence’s departure for Inter Milan.

On Udogie, Tonali told Stadium Astro: "He's a lovely guy. He's I think he's one of the best left wing[-backs]. He has to work every day now. He has a little bit of a problem with injuries, but I think he's a good guy for us.

"I think he played one of the best games against Manchester [United], and he pushes up like a high winger, and I love him because he's always happy.

"If you win, he's happy; if you lose, he's happy. If you have a bad day, he's happy, and I think when I look at him, I'm happy.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 18:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:56.

High-flying Cambuur will look to continue their resurgence when they host Sparta Rotterdam at Kooi Stadion on Saturday evening.

On the other hand, the visitors head to Leeuwarden aiming to end a run of consecutive defeats and arrest a slump in form which has seen them lose four of their last five matches.

Like fellow newcomers ADO Den Haag and Willem II, Cambuur made a difficult start to life back in the top flight, collecting just one point from their opening five matches before claiming their first win of the season against NEC on September 12.

Johan Plat’s men have barely looked back since. Saturday’s 3-2 victory over Utrecht was their sixth win in nine matches across all competitions (D2, L1), the second-best record in the division over that period, behind only Ajax.

Now eighth in the Eredivisie table, the Yellow-Blues are closer to the European places than the relegation zone - a prospect that seemed inconceivable after they opened the campaign with four straight defeats by a combined score of 16-4.

Only seven of Cambuur’s 18 points so far have come in home matches, leaving them with much improvement in front of their fans, where November 8’s 5-2 thrashing at the hands of reigning champions PSV Eindhoven marked a fourth defeat in seven outings this term.

Saturday’s hosts are also winless in their last five home matches against Sparta dating back to January 2026 and could only muster one point across both meetings of their most recent Eredivisie campaign in 2022-23, leaving further room for apprehension within the home crowd.

Industry observers note that after winning five consecutive Eredivisie matches either side of the new year, Sparta would have been optimistic about 2026. However, following a tumultuous couple of months, they will now be desperate to avoid ending the year in the bottom three.

Appointed to steady the ship following the departure of long-serving manager Maurice Steijn, Rogier Meijer has yet to spark a turnaround at Het Kasteel, and the former NEC boss is under increasing pressure to improve results.

Sunday’s 5-1 defeat to AZ Alkmaar was Meijer’s heaviest since taking charge in July, with Sparta having now conceded at least twice in 11 consecutive matches, giving them the division’s third-worst defensive record behind Willem II and FC Utrecht.

Only Groningen and Utrecht have scored more than De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren’s 22 goals among the bottom-half teams, so finding the net has not been a problem for Sparta and reducing their defensive frailties could help spark an upturn in form.

In the second of two consecutive away matches against newly-promoted sides, Saturday’s visitors will look to respond to a disappointing 3-1 defeat to ADO Den Haag last time out.

Sparta have scored four of their 15 away goals between the 15th and 30th minute, while Cambuur have conceded seven of their 20 home goals during the same period, giving Meijer’s men a prime window of opportunity to strike.

Jamal Amofa is expected to miss the rest of the season after suffering a cruciate ligament injury in October.

Twenty-four-year-old Jorn Berkhout was left out of the matchday squad against Utrecht due to injury, making his involvement on Saturday uncertain.

Nicolas Binder and Ilyes Hamache have each scored in three of Cambuur’s last five league matches and will be key to the hosts’ attacking threat.

Bruno Martins Indi is ineligible to feature for Sparta after he was sent off for two bookable offences six minutes apart against AZ.

He joins fellow defenders Teo Quintero and Nick Verschuren as the visitors continue to suffer from defensive absentees, which have plagued their season to date.

First-choice goalkeeper Michael Brouwer was absent last time out, so Filip Bednarek, who is averaging a 52% save accuracy, looks on course to deputise once again.

Arsenal are also mentioned to be interested in young Paris Saint-Germain full-back David Boly, although a move for the talented 17-year-old could be difficult to pull off.

Elsewhere, the Gunners could look to strengthen at left wing after letting Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard leave over the summer.

Christos Tzolis made a bright start after arriving from Club Brugge, but the Greek winger has not scored or assisted since returning from injury at the start of November.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • He was visibly more subdued this time, wearing the look of a man who’d spent two months contemplating the prospect of a jail stretch, whilst the contemporaries he once stood with in the England squad, Harry Kane, Jordan Henderson and Jordan Pickford, were continuing to hit the heights.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By IAN HERBERT - DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:21 EST, 25 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 25 November 2026.

Raheem Sterling wore black to his sentencing hearing today, just as he had when he arrived at Basingstoke Magistrates Court two months ago and admitted to 90 minutes of terrifying rush hour driving, with canisters of nitrous oxide on the passenger seat beside him.

He was visibly more subdued this time, wearing the look of a man who’d spent two months contemplating the prospect of a jail stretch, whilst the contemporaries he once stood with in the England squad, Harry Kane, Jordan Henderson and Jordan Pickford, were continuing to hit the heights.

According to recent reports, imprisonment was only ever a narrow possibility under the sentencing guidelines for dangerous driving, given the miracle that Sterling did not cause serious injury or worse as he zig-zagged between lanes on the M3 and M4 that morning last May. Critically, he was not found to be under the influence of nitrous oxide. A motorist who drove in equally erratic fashion and initially ignored police on Cheshire’s M56, in a BMW which had only three tyres, was handed a suspended sentence earlier this year.

But while the mitigation preceding the magistrate’s decision that Sterling would walk free - his 12-month prison sentence is suspended for 18 months - garlanded him for his charity work and promotion of racial equality, don’t let it be said that his conduct that day was anything less than a disgrace. The tetchy hyper sensitivity Sterling displayed with the police officers who arrested him revealed a shocking lack of contrition and shame.

Industry observers note that sterling has had his challenges, of course. The early death of his father and a nomadic London childhood spent helping his mum on cleaning jobs. But then he disappeared into the cocooned existence of the football academy world, full of the little princes who have people fawning over them, telling them how good they are and throwing obscene amounts of money at them.

Raheem Sterling's conduct the day of his car crash was nothing short of a disgrace.

Sterling's meteoric rise has meant he does not have the tools to deal with rejection.

It has been revealed that kane has flourished in a way that Sterling hasn’t because he was forced to learn the hard way, deal with rejection and develop a sense of perspective. The princes are at the mercy of the hangers on and leeches, around them for a cut of their next substantial pay cheque. It was Sterling’s misfortune to select Aidy Ward as his agent – the man who conducted ugly, public contract negotiations with Liverpool which included declaring that Sterling wouldn’t be staying at Anfield even if he were offered nearly £1m a week. The reputational damage that caused Sterling should have seen him sack Ward on the spot.

It has been revealed that the problem for those whose adolescence takes place in football’s gilded cage is that they combust and can’t hack it when the going gets remotely tough. For Sterling, read Dele Alli, Kalvin Phillips and Aaron Ramsdale.

But what makes Sterling’s personal disintegration so needless is that he really has had positive influences around him in the background. Friends who were there when he wanted to develop a voice to speak against racial discrimination in football. There when he wanted to establish a Foundation to help the kind of London teenagers that he used to be.

According to recent reports, he lost those influences during the chaotic descent into the insanity of that spring morning when he went berserk in his car. Some of them have described to me how he flatly refused to respond to calls and went into ‘oblivion mode’ in the hours after his arrest. It seemed like he was seeking escape from any vestige of the game which is all he has known.

England captain and Sterling's former team-mate Harry Kane has thrived due to the early setbacks in his career.

The tragedy is Sterling has a strong support network who want the best for him.

According to recent reports, the bleak reality for Sterling is that his career in football is surely over now. Yes, he could pick up the thread in some place below the Premier League, though his unhappy experience at Feyenoord – where there was a prurient fascination with his struggles – suggests that he will face the same relentless scrutiny wherever he goes. In the modern world, more gratuitous pleasure than ever is taken in the fall of those who were once great. It will be a circus if he pitches up somewhere newly introduced.

But the evidence of that work with boys in London suggests that he has far more of a hinterland to turn to than Alli and his ilk, if only he can re-establish those positive influences and seek help.

Industry observers note that A moment in time, precisely two years ago, proves what his future might look like. At a meeting room in King's Cross, Sterling sat with a group of seven young men, all of whom were deemed at risk of drifting into knife crime and who had been sent along to his foundation by Brent's youth offending service.

According to recent reports, after an initial 15 or 20 minutes when the boys seemed blinded by the superstar in their midst, they became more comfortable, seeming to feel he understood the likes of them. There were smiles as he described the various school social groups he knew. 'The cool group, the middle of the road group and the geeks,' as he called them. The 'geeks' always seemed to be a bigger part of his world when exams approached, he remarked with a grin. The room was wreathed with laughter, then.

According to recent reports, the group session evolved into several one-to-one conversations between him and the boys who'd been more reticent. It was then that he pointed out the value of allowing outside mentors to help you, if your home life is challenging. 'Having someone else involved changed the course of my life,' Sterling told them.

According to recent reports, now is the moment when Sterling needs others to help change the course of his own life and if he accepts that, he could play a part in public life again. First comes the challenge of rousing himself from any lingering self-pity, emerging from the celebrity bubble and appreciating that he is supremely lucky to remain a free man after those abominable, mindless few hours in his souped-up car.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin has shut down all rumours of a Leeds United exit by signing a upcoming contract at Elland Road.

The striker had been linked with a move away from the Yorkshire club - with several outlets identifying him as a potential target for Manchester United - but he will remain a White after penning a newly introduced two-and-a-half-year deal.

The No9 has spent the past two seasons at Leeds, joining Daniel Farke’s side upon their return to the Premier League last term.

He has established himself as the club’s first-choice striker since his free transfer move after his contract at Everton expired at the end of the 2024-25 campaign.

The England international has forced his way into Thomas Tuchel’s intends for the most recent Nations League games, and he could well have a chance to impress up top with Harry Kane sidelined after tearing his ankle ligaments.

Calvert-Lewin netted 15 goals in his first season in a Leeds shirt, and he has six strikes in 13 matches so far this term.

His hot run of goalscoring form has seen him linked with a move to Old Trafford, where new manager Mauricio Pochettino is thought to be keen on reinforcing his attack after injuries to Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford.

Calvert-Lewin was one of the names that was reportedly on the Red Devils’ shortlist ahead of the January transfer window, but his decision to sign a new contract at Elland Road will come as a major blow to Pochettino as he looks to shape United’s squad in his image.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crystal Palace delivered Thomas Frank a first victory after they came back to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.

Dean Henderson was kept busy in the first half, making several stops to ensure it was all to play for after the break in south London, where Frank took charge of a home game for the first time.

Mamadou Sarr broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, but the contest turned on its head when Jon Martin was sent off with a second yellow card six minutes later.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired in the penalty before second-half substitute Dwight McNeil tapped home from Jorgen Strand Larsen’s overhead kick.

Yeremy Pino had a chance to put the game away with a stoppage-time penalty but he was denied by Unai Marrero, and the hosts had to grind out a nervy finish.

The result moves the Eagles into a play-off position, after starting the evening just outside of it, in 25th.

Frank once again elected to employ a back four, as he did in his first game in charge, their 3-2 Premier League loss at Coventry.

The first chance came after a cagey first 10 minutes when the hosts gave the ball away and it fell to Benat Turrientes, who drew Henderson into a save from distance.

Henderson was then called back into action, twice denying the ever-threatening Goncalo Guedes, who was teed up by Mikel Oyarzabal’s through ball.

Palace’s best opportunity came on the stroke of half-time via a Richards throw-in, glanced on by Axel Disasi and nodded over by Mateta.

Henderson made his fifth save of the night, reacting promptly to deny Jon Gorrotxategi, and the visitors remained in the driver’s seat as the hour approached and Frank made his first substitution, replacing Eddie Nketiah with McNeil.

The breakthrough for Sociedad was the product of a patient build-up ending in Job Ochieng’s low pass for Sarr, who tapped it home.

Industry observers note that the sides were level six minutes later. Palace were awarded a penalty after Martin – who was shown a second yellow card – tugged down Mateta, and the France striker made no mistake, burying the ball past Unai Marrero.

McNeil’s winner was the product of another acrobatic assist from fellow substitute Strand Larsen, whose scorpion kick teed up Pino at Coventry.

This time it was an overhead kick, which was heading wide of the goal but McNeil pounced at the post to poke it home.

Palace were awarded a second penalty when Soler was charged with a handball, but Marrero was equal to it, giving the visitors a fighting chance at a last-gasp leveller.

But Henderson produced his biggest save of the night, denying Orri Oskarsson at the death to preserve a much-needed Palace win.

Nico Paz is open to joining Manchester United next summer and does not favour a return to Real Madrid, according to reports.

The 22-year-old joined Madrid in 2016 but made only eight first-team appearances before he made the move to Como two years ago.

During his time in Italy, Paz has played a pivotal role in Como’s rise, scoring 25 goals and registering 25 assists in 91 appearances for the Serie A club.

Paz has also delivered several impressive performances in the Champions League this season, including a man-of-the-match display in Como’s 4-1 win over Manchester United.

Earlier this month, reports in Spain claimed that Real Madrid intend to activate their €80 million (£67m) buyback clause to re-sign Paz from Como next summer.

Madrid did have the option to re-sign Paz this year but the midfielder personally requested to stay at Como for another season.

‘I thought this was where I would grow the most. I think I made the right decision and I’m happy I did,’ Paz remarked in September.

However, The Athletic reports that Paz ‘does not currently favour re-joining Madrid’ and the midfielder has not yet been given any assurances over playing time if he does return.

The report adds that Paz is on United’s shortlist of candidates to replace Bruno Fernandes, whose contract expires next summer but the club have the option to extend it for a further year.

“He then added that obviously it will be up to him to decide what he wants to do with his career, but also that in Rome the people would go crazy for him, the fans would go crazy for him and his teammates would also be very happy to welcome him.

“So Endrick has also received messages from the Brazilians on the Roma side. On the other hand, we must never forget Milan in the matter because we know that the Diavolo are very attentive to the Endrick situation and also that Gerry Cardinale is directly involved.

“Milan are absolutely keeping its antennas up, waiting to see what will happen. All the various possibilities, however, pass through Real Madrid and José Mourinho.”.

The games Carlos Baleba will miss as Mauricio Pochettino reveals full extent of injury blow

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year with Mauricio Pochettino revealing the full extent of his injury blow.
  • Baleba was forced off in the second-half of United’s Champions League clash against Roma on 3 November with a hamstring injury.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United midfielder Carlos Baleba will not play again this year with Mauricio Pochettino revealing the full extent of his injury blow.

Baleba was forced off in the second-half of United’s Champions League clash against Roma on 3 November with a hamstring injury.

The former Brighton star made a bursting run into the box but pulled up just as he was about to shoot on goal and appeared to be in tears as he limped off the Old Trafford pitch.

Baleba has not featured since with Michael Carrick explaining in the days that followed: ‘We don’t know exactly, but it’ll be a number of weeks.

Recent findings suggest that ‘It’s definitely not this week and it won’t be any time over the international break. It’ll be a little bit longer than that.’.

Carrick has since been replaced by Pochettino at Old Trafford but the Argentine will not get the chance to work with Baleba just yet.

Asked for an update on the Cameroon international, Pochettino revealed he would be sidelined for 10-12 weeks, dating back to when the injury first occurred.

That timescale rules him out of the entire festive period and possibly until the end of January.

Brentford (H) – 28 NovemberNewcastle (A) – 2 DecemberCoventry (H) – 5 DecemberRB Leipzig (H) – 8 DecemberCrystal Palace (A) – 13 DecemberArsenal (A) – 20 DecemberNottingham Forest (H) – 27 DecemberSunderland (H) – 30 DecemberBrighton (A) – 2 JanuaryNewcastle (H) – 7 JanuaryFA Cup third round – TBC – 9 January.

Aston Villa (A) – 16 JanuaryBayern Munich (H) – 20 JanuaryLiverpool (H) – 24 JanuaryVillarreal (A) – 27 January.

‘He was injured against Roma, medical people were talking about 10-12 weeks,’ Pochettino told a press conference on Friday.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

According to recent reports, united have eight games left in 2026 starting with the visit of Brentford on Saturday. They then head to Newcastle United midweek before back-to-back home games against Coventry City and RB Leipzig.

They are on the road again in mid-December against Crystal Palace, staying in the capital for their final game before Christmas against Arsenal on 20 December.

United next take on Nottingham Forest and Sunderland before beginning the new year against Baleba’s old club Brighton on 2 January.

Baleba could also miss United’s FA Cup third game against an opponent to be decided and January games against Newcastle, Aston Villa, Bayern Munich and the home game against Liverpool.
